Talking Heads The Democratic Circus - Seemed Appropriate for season

In 1993 I drove a 1974 Chevy K5 Blazer that I would remove the top from and drive around as a convertible in the summer months. I was in my late 20's I had money in my pocket, I lived in a Ski Town and was a Bachelor. Life was grand. I had a job at the local paper where I worked nights where I layed out the paper, Toward the end of Summer the tourism would knock off, it was not Summer but also it was not Winter. We called it shoulder season. The town was reduced to a thousand or so people and this wasn't a lot considering the population on the 4th of July Weekend or Christmas Holiday was around 50,000 people.

So the boss would ask me if I would help out in slow times and deliver some of the papers to the local businesses? You got it! I would respond. This was to be done early on Thursday mornings so the papers would be there first thing in the morning. I picked them up at 2:15 AM and I would be back home usually by 4:30AM. Our town was small. Two by Two square miles and because it was a small town where the bars closed at 10pm with one staying open until midnight, it was pretty much just me out and about in the early hours. I would see one other human, he was sweeping the parking lots with one of those vacuum trucks.

I would load up the Blazer with the papers, with the top off it was great because they were easy to reach and I would start my rounds So what has this got to do with the Talking Heads? I love music and everything I do has a soundtrack. For some strange reason I associate this album with delivering papers on one of those nights. I would have the music on, loud enough to hear it, but not so loud it might cause a disturbance. Since it was so quiet out, my stereo had the volume low. Hearing this album brings back the memories. I can smell the pine pollen and feel the warm summer breeze that blows through the Sierra in September.

I no longer live in that town, and I miss it terribly. Shoulder seasons no longer exist. Tourism is year round and the paper is no longer. The town is home to a year round population closer to 8,000 and all the bars stay open as late as they can. I do have a nice life now with a family and I own a home. There are moments I wish I could go back to those bachelor days just for an hour or two where I play music loud and not worry about responsibilities. My concerns were, Jet Ski tomorrow or ride Dirt Bikes? Why not both?

Perhaps we all wish we could go back to comfort times in our lives if just for an hour or two.
